text.p: Michael Tucker had five hits and five RBI and Fred McGriff homered twice and drove in five runs as the Atlanta Braves posted their major-league record 19th win in April with a 12-3 rout of the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday.
Tucker had four singles and his second homer of the season, a three-run shot in the eighth.
"It's a lot different being with the Braves. When we come to the park everybody knows what they have to do. It's obvious when you walk in, everyone's more relaxed."
Atlanta, which is a major-league best 19-6, surpassed six other teams with 18 victories in April.
Denny Neagle (4-0) won his fourth straight start, allowing three runs and nine hits over seven innings.
At Colorado, Larry Walker tied a National League record with his 11th April homer and Andres Galarraga added his eighth career grand slam as the Colorado Rockies routed the Chicago Cubs 11-5.
Walker, who went 2-for-4 with three RBI, gave the Rockies a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the fourth inning with his league-leading 11th homer of the year.
His homer total in the opening month tied the league record set by Gary Sheffield and Barry Bonds, who each hit 11 last April.
I'm happy it happened but I'm more happy that we won the game," Walker said. "We have a lot of games left, so I'm not that excited."
In Montreal, David Segui hit a three-run homer and drove in four runs as the Montreal Expos snapped a three-game losing streak with an 8-6 victory over the Houston Astros.
Segui's three-run blast, his fourth homer of the year, off Astros starter Darryl Kile in the fourth inning gave Montreal the lead for good. He added an RBI single in the fifth inning.
Mark Grudzielanek singled in the first inning to extend his hitting streak to 15 games.

In New York, Bobby Jones allowed a pair of runs over six innings and Carlos Baerga came off the bench to add two key hits and score twice as the New York Mets handed the San Diego Padres their eighth straight loss 6-2.
Jones (4-2) allowed six hits, walked two and struck out six for the Mets, who have won four straight games.
"I think we are a better team than our record shows," Jones said. "Things are coming together."

In Philadelphia, Todd Zeile's run-scoring single snapped a sixth-inning tie and Hideo Nomo ended his two-game losing streak as the Los Angeles Dodgers won consecutive games for the first time in two weeks with a 7-5 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies.

"I've really started out the season struggling," said Zeile, who went 2-for-4 to raise his batting average to .175. "I'm just glad to get some RBI tonight. I'm just trying to relax and let things happen. That's what you have to do in this game."
Nomo (3-2) went 6 1/3 innings, allowing three runs and six hits.

In Pittsburgh, Mark Gardner threw a three-hitter and tied a career high with 11 strikeouts and Jeff Kent added a first-inning grand slam as the San Francisco Giants defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 6-1.
Gardner allowed just one run and didn't walk a batter. He struck out 11 -- seven looking.

In St Louis, Willie McGee's two-run triple highlighted a five-run fifth inning as the St. Louis Cardinals extended their season-high winning streak to four games with a 6-2 victory over the Florida Marlins.
"McGee's triple was a quality and clutch piece of hitting," said St. Louis manager Tony La Russa.

"I got a good look at the ball and jumped on it at the right time," McGee said. "I did not realise that I was going to have the opportunity for a triple until I turned second and saw Lach (Rene Lachemann) wave me on."
